text.p: In world commodity markets on Friday night, the copper market ended on a buoyant note and helped to instil a more confident tone to some of the other base metals.
Gold prices fell slightly while wheat prices jumped on concerns about U.S. weather. Oil prices spiked on shorcovering.
The CRB index closed up 1.87 points at 246.93.
Most LME metals displayed a firmer tone on Friday afternoon but zinc was the only metal that ventured out of familiar ranges ahead of Third Wednesday pricing next week.

Three months copper ended modestly firmer, but still well within the week's range of $2,312-$2,375 after stocks data showed a 4,275-tonne draw. It finished the afternoon kerb $17 higher at $2,356 per tonne, and may be preparing to resume probes to the upside.
Zinc steamed ahead to a fresh high since October 1992, touching $1,292, buoyed by a stocks decline of 3,425 tonnes and fresh speculative buying.
Aluminium finished the day slightly higher at $1,668, up $10 after inventories fell by 1,750 tonnes.
Nickel briefly tested the upper end of its recent range, hitting $8,140, but drifted back to close $55 higher at $8,115.
Lead was the only metal to end in the negative column, shedding $3 to finish the day at $690.
Tin closed $10 higher at $6,060 with chartists noting the bullish cross of the 10-day and 30-day moving averages. Alloy finished stronger at $1,550, up $10.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended lower Friday, on moderate volumes, ahead of the expiry of April gold, silver and platinum options at the close. COMEX April gold ended down $1.50 at $352.90 an ounce, after trading a $355.50-352.50 range. Estimated total gold futures volume was 25,000 lots. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $352.00/352.50, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $352.80 and the New York close Thursday around $353.10/60. Spot gold prices have drifted in a $350-355 range this week, after a month-long recovery from three year lows around $336, driven by funds covering near-record short positions.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on concerns about adverse weather in U.S. areas where the three main classes of wheat are grown, traders said. Wheat closed seven to 10-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 9-1/4 at $3.83-1/4. Gains in March were limited by news Sri Lanka bought wheat from Argentina and the EU rather than from the U.S. Also a Philippine firm rejected offers on U.S. wheat and soybeans.

NYMEX crude futures ended sharply higher on Friday, partly on short covering ahead of an annual industry event beginning Sunday and buying in the front calender spread. April settled up 59 cents at $21.29 a barrel. Traders also noted the expiry in the April crude options also buoyed the front month with buying seen in the $21.00 and $21.50 strikes.
